metadata.note: The Pittsburg, Shawmut and Northern (the charter spells it 'Pittsburg', no h; nickname 'Shawmut Line') ran from Wayland and Hornell, NY, through Angelica, Bolivar and Olean to Smethport, St. Marys and Brockwayville, PA. Its New York end began as the 3-ft Allegany Central (Olean - Bolivar - Angelica, 1881) and passed through the Lackawanna and Pittsburgh (1883), Lackawanna and Southwestern (1889) and Central New York and Western (1892) before the 1899 PS&N consolidation, so Olean - Bolivar is split into five features and Bolivar - Angelica's narrow-gauge era into two, all sharing geometry, each in its operating company's colour (Rule 4; boundary years shared, as in west_shore_railroad.geojson). The 1905-1946 receivership is not a split. Public passenger service ended January 5 1938 (Robinson 1943); the road ran freight only until April 1 1947, which is not drawn. Research report: research/branches/pittsburgh_shawmut_and_northern_railroad.txt.

not_yet_sourced: PENNSYLVANIA END DATES (UNRESOLVED 1): Prosser - Smethport - St. Marys drawn to 1930 [OPEN] on Wikipedia's citation of a February 1930 Official Guide that was not seen; St. Marys - Brockwayville drawn to 1927 [OPEN] on an unsourced ACHS editor's note. Conflicting: passenger service 'discontinued entirely in 1935' (GAS editor's note); Robinson's 'past eight or ten years' (c.1928-1935). A 1930-35 Official Guide or Fowler's branchline.uk Pennsylvania file would settle it.
New York end: Robinson's Jan 5 1938 (used) vs the GAS editor's note's 1935 (UNRESOLVED 2).

Every start year is a first CONFIRMED year, not an opening: 1882 [OPEN] for the Allegany Central lines; 1905 [OPEN] for Bolivar - Angelica (rebuilt 1902-3), Angelica - Wayland, the Hornell Branch and all Pennsylvania lines (through route complete c.1902).
Single-year 1905 [ANCHOR]s: Mount Jewett Branch, Kersey Branch, Clarion River Division - no other year confirmed.
Bolivar - Angelica narrow gauge end: 'shortly after' May 7 1889, i.e. 1889-1890; drawn to 1889.

Pre-1910 routing State Line - Coryville over the PRR (Robinson p.82) is drawn as its own feature 1905-1909; where the trains joined the PRR at State Line, and whether any ran Olean - Eldred over the PRR throughout, is not established.
Hornell Branch mileage 14 / 11 / 9 (UNRESOLVED 9) and its Hornell terminal; the last 2 mi into Hornell are approximate.
Mount Jewett Branch traced about 15% short of 10-10.54 mi; location of 'Gallup' not established.
P&S lease start: Robinson Feb 1 1908 vs Wikipedia 1906 vs CHRON '1908 to 1916' (UNRESOLVED 7) - affects only the undrawn block [12].

segments.note: 3 ft gauge. Olean RR (inc. May 2 1881) built Olean - Bolivar, completed 'autumn of 1881' (Robinson p.76); consolidated into the Allegany Central Nov 21 1881. Starts at 1882 [OPEN]: 1882 is the first CONFIRMED year (Allegany Central timetable, Wellsville Daily Reporter Feb 15 1882: Bradford/Olean - Weston's - Portville - White House - Ceres - Little Genesee - Bolivar - Richburg - ... - Angelica, four trains each way); 1881 service is likely but undated. Ends 1883: the Allegany Central was absorbed by the Lackawanna and Pittsburgh on Mar 24 1883 (Robinson pp.76-82), the split year shared with the next feature. Headway is an ESTIMATE derived from the four trains each way in TT1882.

segments.note: Pittsburg, Shawmut and Northern from the Aug 1899 consolidation; Prosser - Olean became the PS&N 'Olean Branch'. Standard-gauged Dec 27 1901 (Robinson p.83). Confirmed 1901 (PS&N timetable effective Oct 14 1901: Bolivar - Olean with Riverhurst, two to three each way), 1905 (TT1905; Robinson p.83: two trains daily Hornell - Olean and four Olean Branch locals), 1926 (TT1926, 'additional passenger train service' Olean - Bolivar - Richburg - Angelica, trains 9/10, 13/14, 15/16) and 1935 (TT1935, train 9/10 Olean - Wayland, daily except Sunday). In receivership from Aug 1 1905 (trusteeship 1946) - the same company ran the trains, so not a split. In the last years the only service was a daily mixed train Olean - Wayland - Hornell (Robinson p.84); mixed trains carry passengers. 'Public passenger service was discontinued January 5, 1938' (Robinson p.84), so the segment ends 1938; freight continued to Apr 1 1947 and is not drawn. Conflict recorded: the ACHS editor's note (GAS) says passenger service ended 'entirely in 1935'; Robinson, writing in 1943 from personal knowledge of the line and giving an exact date, is preferred. Headway is an ESTIMATE for the middle years (two to four trains); by the 1930s it was one mixed train each way.
sources: Segment-level: start at the Aug 1899 PS&N consolidation (Robinson pp.81-83); service confirmed by PS&N timetables of Oct 14 1901, Jan 15 1905, Apr 25 1926 and June 16 1935; end at the Jan 5 1938 discontinuance (Robinson p.84). Headway is an estimate.

Starts at 1905 [OPEN]: 1905 is the first CONFIRMED passenger year (PS&N time card effective Jan 15 1905, TT1905, and Robinson's 1905 public timetable summary, p.83); service may well have begun earlier but no earlier year is confirmed. Drawn to 1930 [OPEN]: 1930 is the last year with positive evidence, and that evidence is Wikipedia's citation of a 1930 Official Guide which has NOT been seen for this layer.
